How slow can you make the LED blink? Try 2000 milliseconds.

The code talks. The board listens.

Johnny-Five turns actions like led.blink(500) into Firmata messages. A simulated Arduino runs the same firmware a real board would, receives those messages, and changes its pins. Here, both sides run in your browser.

The built-in LED is connected to pin 13. An external LED needs a complete path from an output pin, through a resistor and the LED, back to GND. A button and a dial send information in the other direction.

This lab uses a simplified circuit model: it shows connections and pin behavior, but does not calculate current, component damage, or all physical effects.

Built for curious minds. No hardware needed.
Read JavaScript on Things

A little lab, open to everyone.

Explore JavaScript and electronics without buying a board. Paste Johnny-Five code, connect virtual components, and experiment.

The app uses the real Johnny-Five library, AVR8js processor emulation, real Firmata firmware, and Wokwi’s component visuals. AVR8js is also the Arduino engine used by Velxio. This is an independent learning app.

Start with LEDs, buttons, analog inputs, and servos. Some Johnny-Five devices need additional firmware or a component model that this lab does not include. Native Node.js modules, package installation, and a terminal are not available.

Your code runs locally in a worker. Stop terminates it and resets the board. Projects are saved on this device. Shared links include the code and circuit; opening a link never runs it automatically.

The experiments are original examples. The book link is a reading companion; this app is not affiliated with Manning, Arduino, Wokwi, or Velxio.
